learning: Iteration 3 left one s-bend line loss per run at 16 mm footprints. Whether the 12 mm footprint removes it is the question for the next race. If it does not, the row should move back (y below 0.03 m), not forward, because iteration 2 showed forward raised max_error.
notes: Adopts the Builder's 12 mm footprint at the ±0.08 m span and y=0.03 m row. The controller is held at iteration 3 values so the footprint change is isolated.
rationale: Iteration 3 (±0.08 m span, 16 mm footprints, y=0.03 m, 0.6 kg, kp 8.0) kept oval max_error at 0.0608 m with zero line losses, and the slalom had zero line losses. The s-bend still lost the line once per run (max_error 0.0656 m), and the score fell from 65.32 to 50.65. Iteration 2 showed that moving the row forward (y=0.05 m) raised oval max_error to 0.0637 m and brought back slalom line losses, so the row stays at y=0.03 m. The Builder's proposal changes only sensor_size from 0.016 to 0.012 m, keeping the ±0.08 m span and the mass at 0.6 kg. I keep the controller identical to iteration 3 (kp 8.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.8, weights ±2 at 25 per metre, last_direction) so that the footprint is the only change the race can attribute. The Builder's requested sum-of-readings and loss-step measurements are not in the allowed observation set, so I request the closest allowed measurements (line_loss_events, max_error, steering_oscillation). Expected result: line_loss_events falls to zero on the s-bend and slalom, and max_error returns near 0.061 m on the oval. This is an expectation, not a measured result. Iteration 0 used 12 mm footprints with a narrower span, so the footprint's effect at ±0.08 m is not yet tested.
